collection.description: A child thinks pieces of the moon have gone missing.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (child) thinks pieces of the moon have gone missing.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: (adult), a researcher, explains that sunlight lights different parts of the moon.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: (child) learns the moon is still whole.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: (child) draws the moon on clear nights.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: Cloudy nights leave gaps in the drawings.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: (elder) tells a traditional story without calling it proof.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: (child) compares the story with observed phases.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: A torch and round object help demonstrate changing illumination.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: (child) finds the model confusing and asks to try again.
